newsitem.title: INDIA: India CBI says to end CRB group enquiry in August.
newsitem.headline: India CBI says to end CRB group enquiry in August.

text.p: The chief of India's federal police on Friday moved back the estimated date of completion of an inquiry into the failed CRB group of companies, saying it would end by August 20.
"The CBI part of the case should be over by August 15," Joginder Singh, the director of India's Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told reporters in Bombay.
On May 30, Singh had said he expected the investigation to be completed within a month's time. He gave no reason for the delay.
Singh said investigations in India would be tied up by August, but tracking down leads overseas might take longer.
"The investigation will be completed within the statutory period of three months required by the law," Singh added. "The case was registered on May 20."

The CRB group of companies, a financial services provider whose business interests also spanned textiles and building materials, failed late in May taking the savings of thousands of investors with it.
Business and political circles are still reeling from the collapse. Federal police set the firm's liabilities at 9.32 billion rupees.

The firm's chairman C.R. Bhansali, who has been in the custody of the CBI since Monday, has said he wants to return the investors' money. CBI officials are questioning him in a bid to lay bare his group's business activities.
Singh said the CBI had not recovered any of the money so far. Asked if the missing funds had been spirited abroad, Singh replied, "We have still to find it out."

Singh refused to discuss the details of Bhansali's interrogation. "I'm not going to mention any part of the interrogation," he said. "Anything more would affect and be prejudicial to the investigation."

Singh said he was in Bombay for discussions with the probe committee which has representatives from the Maharashtra state police, the revenue and income tax departments, the central bank and market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
